newsitem.title: INDIA: India alliance says resolved DMK withdrawal threat.
newsitem.headline: India alliance says resolved DMK withdrawal threat.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition has resolved its problem linked to a threat by the regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) to withdraw from the government, the alliance's spokesman said on Thursday.
"I would say it is solved," spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters after a four-hour meeting of senior leaders of the coalition, including the DMK's president, Muthuvel Karunanidhi.

The DMK said earlier this week it planned to withdraw its four ministers from the coalition government because the alliance had compromised on its dignity through its internal squabbles and the secret agenda of some members.

The Standing Committee of senior leaders decided not to admit to the coalition a breakaway group of Gujral's Janata Dal party, the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), whose entry was opposed by the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M).
DMK leaders had criticised the communist demand as an interference in the affairs of the Janata Dal, but Karunanidhi accepted the Standing Committee's decision.
"When the DMK became a party to a decision of the Standing Committee, how does the question of the resignation still remain?" Reddy said.
The crisis that began on Monday reversed a rally in Indian stock markets.
